findings.title: Handle an unset embed_category before indexing the query result
findings.body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category is unset, blank, or names a deleted category. The migration indexes the first row before checking whether a category was found, so it raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This blocks upgrades for sites that have never configured embedding, as well as fresh database migrations. The fallback query also needs to tolerate a missing site-setting row.

findings.title: Normalize legacy hosts when migrating them
findings.body: The old embedding configuration accepted entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://discourse.org, but this migration inserts those strings unchanged using SQL, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value with URI.host, which contains neither a scheme nor a path. Consequently, previously working scheme-prefixed hosts stop authorizing embeds and topic retrieval after the upgrade. Normalize migrated entries using the same rules as newly saved hosts before deleting the old setting.

findings.title: Allow valid hosts with longer or internationalized TLDs
findings.body: The hostname validator restricts the final label to two through five ASCII letters. Valid domains such as example.technology and domains with punycode TLDs therefore cannot be added or edited. The previous hostname lookup imposed no such restriction, so this also prevents administrators from saving some migrated hosts. Use hostname validation that accommodates valid DNS labels rather than this limited TLD pattern.

findings.title: Make accepted port-qualified hosts match incoming URLs
findings.body: The validator accepts and stores port-qualified hosts such as example.com:8080, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host from an incoming URL. For http://example.com:8080/article that value is example.com, so the saved entry can never match. The UI reports a successful save while embedding and topic retrieval remain denied. Either normalize away ports consistently or include the port in the lookup according to the intended authorization rules.

findings.title: Prevent conflicting category mappings for the same host
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration's table definition enforces host uniqueness, so administrators can save two entries for the same hostname with different categories. Host lookup uses only the first matching row, silently ignoring the other mapping even though both appear as successfully configured in the UI. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname, including a database constraint, so each host has an unambiguous destination category.
